descriptions.proactive:
Send a short written report about {Product}'s tools to the {Product} team. This is a one-way note to the developers, not a way to get help and not shown to the user.

Use it when, while doing the user's task with {Product}'s tools, one of these happened:
- broken: a tool returned an error, or wrong or incomplete results, for input that matched its schema.
- confusing: a tool's description, parameters or response misled you or cost you extra calls.
- missing: the task needed a capability or data that {Product}'s tools don't offer.
- idea: one specific change would have made this task clearly easier.

Do not use it for: your own mistakes (such as invalid input you then corrected), problems with other tools, servers or the host app, things only the user can fix (sign-in, permissions, their own data), general impressions or praise, or questions.

Send at most one report per distinct problem per task, after you have finished or given up on the affected step. Write for an engineer who cannot see this conversation. Describe inputs in general terms. Never include private information in any parameter. Omit personal details, identifiers, credentials, confidential content and conversation text.

The reply is only an acknowledgement. Continue the user's task either way and never retry this tool.
descriptions.conservative:
Send a short written report about {Product} to the {Product} team. This is a one-way note to the developers, not a way to get help.

Use it only when:
- the user asks you to report a problem or pass feedback to {Product}, or
- a {Product} tool clearly failed or could not do what the user asked, and you have already told the user so.

Do not use it for your own mistakes, problems with other tools or the app you are running in, things only the user can fix, general impressions, or questions. Send at most one report per problem.

Write for an engineer who cannot see this conversation. Describe inputs in general terms. Never include private information in any parameter. Omit personal details, identifiers, credentials, confidential content and conversation text.

The reply is only an acknowledgement. Continue helping the user either way and never retry this tool.

fields.kind: Which of the four cases this is. Pick the closest one.
fields.summary: One sentence an engineer could use as an issue title. Name the tool and the symptom. Good: 'search_orders returns an empty list when status is "refunded"'. Bad: 'search doesn't work'. Omit private information.
fields.goal: What the user was trying to accomplish with {Product}'s tools. Paraphrase in one general sentence and omit private information.
fields.impact: blocked: could not complete the step. worked_around: completed it another way. friction: completed it, but it cost extra calls or guesses.
fields.tool: Use only the registered {Product} tool name. Omit it if none applies or the name contains private information.
fields.actual: For a broken tool, summarize the error or the shape of the result. Omit private information and avoid pasting raw messages or output.
fields.expected: Describe the expected result in general terms, without private information.
fields.suggestion: Suggest the smallest change that would have helped, if you have one. Omit private information.
fields.requested_by_user: True only if the user explicitly asked you to send this feedback.

results.success: Recorded for the {Product} team (ref {report_id}). Continue with the user's task. Nothing else is needed and you should not call this tool again for the same problem.
results.failure: The report could not be recorded right now. That's fine: continue with the user's task and do not retry.
